candidates.name: vegas-tourism-insights
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit analytics app with a committed 'LVCVA Data.xlsx' (cleaned) in data/, sourced from official Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority releases. Fields per README: visitor volume, room nights occupied, occupancy rate, ADR, RevPAR, auto traffic on major highways, room tax collections. Includes a Jupyter notebook for cleaning/EDA and manual forecasts extending to June 2025. Exact year range not stated in README but framed as 'historical tourism trends' (multi-year monthly).
candidates.why_useful: Las Vegas is a top-10 US Airbnb/STR market and LVCVA publishes some of the best public monthly visitor-volume + ADR + RevPAR + hotel occupancy data among US destinations; a pre-cleaned, committed spreadsheet mirror saves re-scraping LVCVA's site and gives a monthly hotel-market comparator for Airbnb NA nights/ADR (addresses gap #8, hotel supply/demand benchmarking, and gap #2 realised ADR/occupancy analogue).
candidates.time_coverage: multi-year monthly (exact start/end not confirmed from README)

candidates.name: Forecasting-Las-Vegas-Visitor-Volume-Time-Series-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Time-series forecasting notebook for Las Vegas visitor volume; README states the dataset is 'publicly available at the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority' research portal (external link) rather than a committed file — could not confirm whether raw CSV is checked into the repo itself.
candidates.why_useful: Second independent pointer to LVCVA visitor-volume data plus a working method (time-series decomposition/forecast) that could be adapted as a hotel-market comparator for ABNB NA nights; lower value than vegas-tourism-insights since the data itself may not be committed.

candidates.name: hawaii-visitor-data-downloader
candidates.what_it_holds: Python script that downloads monthly visitor statistical report PDFs published by Hawaii DBEDT (Dept. of Business, Economic Development & Tourism). Supports a configurable year range (default 2018-2025), random User-Agent rotation, request delays, auto-retry, skips unavailable months (404), and resumes by skipping already-downloaded files. Output is a folder of DBEDT monthly PDFs, not parsed CSV.
candidates.why_useful: A robust, working one-command puller for Hawaii DBEDT's monthly visitor statistics PDFs going back to 2018 (we already use DBEDT for the party-size series; this tool would let us pull a fuller point-in-time monthly PDF archive rather than only the annual/monthly-highlights pages we currently have via Wayback) — useful for extending or refreshing gap #8 (Hawaii bed-tax/occupancy) and the party-size series baseline.
candidates.size_hint: script only; downloads PDFs, not a stored dataset
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: we already hold Hawaii DBEDT visitor stats per CONTEXT.md; this is a longer/more automatable PDF archive method, not identical data

candidates.name: dvw-data-portal
candidates.what_it_holds: Angular front-end for UHERO's 'DBEDT Visitor Warehouse' (DVW) data portal, serving Hawaii visitor-industry time series (visitor arrivals, spending, room demand/occupancy per public description at data.uhero.hawaii.edu/dvw/). Repo itself is just the Angular CLI app, no data files committed; the actual series live behind the paired dvw-api / data.uhero.hawaii.edu/dvw/ endpoint.
candidates.why_useful: UHERO's DBEDT Visitor Data Warehouse is a more granular, more frequently updated academic mirror of Hawaii tourism data than the DBEDT PDF reports we currently rely on — worth checking data.uhero.hawaii.edu/dvw/ directly for a queryable, possibly monthly/county-level, longer-history series (addresses gap #8 and possibly gap #2 for realised occupancy).
candidates.size_hint: frontend app only; data lives at external data.uhero.hawaii.edu/dvw/ endpoint
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: extends the Hawaii DBEDT visitor stats we already hold with a live, queryable warehouse

candidates.name: dvw-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Go REST API backing DBEDT's visitor data warehouse (paired with dvw-data-portal above). README is sparse/incomplete (no local-dev config, requires production DB connection); does not itself carry data files, but is the API layer over the same DBEDT/UHERO Hawaii visitor warehouse.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms UHERO operates a production API-backed Hawaii tourism data warehouse beyond the static DBEDT reports; if the live API/portal (data.uhero.hawaii.edu/dvw/) is queryable, it could give more granular or more current Hawaii visitor series than we currently hold.
candidates.size_hint: API server code only, no data files

candidates.name: dbedt-data-portal
candidates.what_it_holds: Data portal front-end for DBEDT's *general* data warehouse (broader than just the visitor warehouse — likely covers Hawaii economic indicators generally). Not independently verified beyond the gh search description; likely same architecture as dvw-data-portal.
candidates.why_useful: Possible additional Hawaii macro/economic series (consumer spend, employment) that could serve as a regional demand proxy for Hawaii travel spend, adjacent to gap #6 (consumer spend panels) though for a single state.

candidates.name: kauai
candidates.what_it_holds: "Economic Dashboard for County of Kauai" — county-level Hawaii economic/tourism dashboard by UHERO; likely draws on the same DBEDT visitor warehouse at county granularity (Kauai is a distinct STR/tourism market from Oahu/Maui).
candidates.why_useful: County-level Hawaii breakout (vs. statewide DBEDT figures we hold) would sharpen the Hawaii party-size/occupancy series to a finer geography, useful if Airbnb Hawaii supply is concentrated in specific counties.

notes: This modality's search tooling was largely unusable this run: WebSearch reported its shared session budget already exhausted on the very first call (0 successful WebSearch queries). DuckDuckGo html/lite endpoints returned CAPTCHA or 403 on every attempt. Bing via WebFetch was highly inconsistent: most queries (especially anything with 'visit florida', 'nyc tourism', 'visit orlando', 'visit california', or repeated variants of a prior query) returned obviously generic/cached/irrelevant results (dictionary definitions, Dollar General, AZ quotes, tourism-board homepages) regardless of the site:github.com filter, suggesting either aggressive caching keyed loosely on query similarity or bot-detection soft-blocking that serves decoy SERPs. Only two Bing queries with unusual, highly specific proper-noun phrasing ('DBEDT' hawaii visitor statistics github repository) broke through and returned real, relevant github.com links. github.com/search web pages were 429-rate-limited outright. `gh search repos` (the allowed fallback) worked but hit the authenticated API rate limit twice mid-run (403 'API rate limit exceeded for user ID') even after a 40s backoff, and its full-text multi-word AND matching returned empty for most natural-language phrasings — short, distinctive terms ('lvcva', 'las vegas visitor volume', org:UHERO) worked far better than long descriptive phrases. Net effect: NYC Tourism, Visit Florida, Orlando, Destination DC, and Visit California — five of the seven named agencies in the theme — turned up NO github.com hits in this run despite multiple query attempts each; only Las Vegas (LVCVA) and Hawaii (DBEDT, via UHERO) yielded real candidates. This looks like a genuine scarcity (state/city tourism-board dashboards are rarely mirrored to GitHub) compounded by tooling failures, so a re-run with a working search backend (or `gh search repos` once the API quota resets, using short single/double-word queries and org: filters for likely maintainers like state open-data offices) would likely surface more. Suggest another scout retry NYC (nyc opendata mirrors, e.g. search org:CityOfNewYork or 'nyc-opendata'), Orlando/Destination DC specifically, and broaden to 'airport passenger traffic github csv' and 'transient occupancy tax github' once gh's rate limit clears.
